summary_paragraph: The patient, a male with a history of liver transplant, chronic malnutrition, and recurrent infections, was admitted after his visiting nurse found him hypoxic with a fever. He reported gagging while eating the night before. Imaging and labs confirmed multifocal pneumonia and a urinary tract infection, both due to Pseudomonas aeruginosa. He was treated with intravenous meropenem after initial broad-spectrum coverage. A video swallow study showed no aspiration, allowing resumption of soft solids and thin liquids. His sirolimus dose was reduced from 2 mg to 1 mg daily due to elevated levels. Anemia required one unit of packed red blood cells, and acute kidney injury resolved with IV fluids. He improved clinically, was weaned off supplemental oxygen, and was discharged home on a 14-day course of IV meropenem with home health services and follow-up plans.
